faq_items.question: How much does a litre of spray tan solution cost per treatment?
faq_items.answer: At £60 a litre and 28 treatments to the litre, £2.14 a tan. Your own number will sit either side of that depending on equipment, technique and coverage. Solution is only part of your consumable cost — with disposables, filters and laundry, budget around £3.24 a treatment.

faq_items.question: How many spray tans do you get from a litre?
faq_items.answer: Twenty-eight for the Sunset professional litre. Your own number will sit either side of that depending on equipment, technique and how much of the body you cover. Measure your own: mark the bottle, count the tans over a week, and divide. It's the number every other calculation depends on.

faq_items.question: What profit is there in a spray tan?
faq_items.answer: On a £30 tan with an employed therapist, about £11.30 after consumables, card fees, loaded chair time and a share of fixed costs — roughly 37%. If you do the tans yourself, about £17.65, though that includes what you'd otherwise pay someone. Against an average UK salon margin around 8%, tanning is a strong column.

faq_items.question: Is it worth switching to a cheaper spray tan solution?
faq_items.answer: Probably not. At 12 tans a week, a solution 20% cheaper saves about £267 a year — roughly £5 a week, and the smallest lever in the model. Selling three retail items a week is worth £1,404, and putting £2 on your price is worth £1,229. One lost client from a poor result wipes out the saving.

faq_items.question: How do I work out my overhead per spray tan?
faq_items.answer: Take the fixed costs attributable to the tanning room each month — a share of rent, rates, utilities, insurance and booking software — and divide by the treatments you did that month. At £450 a month and 52 tans, that's £8.65 a tan. The figure falls as you get busier, which is why filling the room is the same thing as making it cheaper.

faq_items.question: What does a spray tan cost to deliver if I'm mobile?
faq_items.answer: The consumables are the same, but travel time, fuel and equipment amortisation change the picture materially, and a no-show costs you the journey as well as the slot. That model is different enough to need its own article.
